tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis: The recorded session starts from about:blank, navigates to the Magento Admin customer URL, logs in via the admin login form, then operates on the Manage Customers grid. It demonstrates: robust login via element indices/hashes, closing an initial notification popup, selecting customers via per-row checkboxes and Select Visible, using mass-action selection links (Select All/Unselect/etc.), performing Actions dropdown operations (Subscribe to Newsletter, Unsubscribe from Newsletter, Assign a Customer Group including the dependent Group selector), and briefly applying a filter and sort. The previous tool failed because it depended on a brittle CSS selector for the username field (input[name="login[username]"][type="text"]) that was not present; this trajectory instead uses deterministic elementHash-based interactions.

2) Task Definition: Create a reusable, deterministic tool that:
- Navigates directly to the admin customer grid URL.
- Logs in with provided credentials using robust selectors (elementHash) rather than fragile CSS.
- Optionally applies a selection strategy (individual selection by first-row checkboxes vs Select Visible) to choose customers.
- Applies a chosen mass action (delete, subscribe, unsubscribe, assign group) via the Actions dropdown and Submit button; when assigning group, also chooses a customer group.
- Optionally applies a simple Group filter and/or sort by Email, as demonstrated, but core focus is mass actions.

3) Action Plan:
- Step 1: navigation to http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/customer/ (login page when not authenticated).
- Step 2–4: deterministic input to the username, password fields and click Login submit button using their elementHash and/or robust cssSelector/xpath from the trajectory.
- Step 5: wait briefly or use an agent step to ensure the Manage Customers grid is loaded (and handle the notification popup via its close link elementHash if present).
- Step 6: perform customer selection:
  - Either click per-row checkboxes (represented by the shared elementHash observed for indices 160–197), or click the Select Visible link (elementHash 0eefac88df) to select all on the page. For a simple deterministic tool, we can parameterize the selection mode (e.g., select_visible vs none vs first_n_rows) but keep the steps linear.
- Step 7: choose mass action via the Actions dropdown (elementHash b202e94e0d on /admin/customer/ and then same on /admin/customer/index/; index 133/136). Use selectedText parameter mapped from tool input (e.g., "Subscribe to Newsletter", "Unsubscribe from Newsletter", "Assign a Customer Group", "Delete").
- Step 8: if action is assign group, select a group from the Group dropdown (elementHash 4a4c64c2db / 547d16e240 / 150) by visible text (e.g., "General", "Wholesale", "VIP Member", "Private Sales Member").
- Step 9: click Submit button (elementHash 32139f0b8f / 94c3ca62f9; indices 134/136/137) to execute mass action.
- Step 10 (optional, but demonstrated): interact with Group filter dropdown (elementHash 547d16e240 when used as filter) and Search button (elementHash 654dbd41a1 – index 128) or click Email header (sorting) via an agent step if deterministic selector is not available. For core tool, we keep one simple deterministic filter interaction (Group filter + Search) as this was explicitly demonstrated.
- Step 11: Optionally extract page content or simply finish; the mass action is server-side and confirmed by a green message, but extraction is not necessary for core functionality.

4) Variable Identification:
Core parameters:
- username (string, required): login username for Magento Admin ("admin" in demonstration but must be parameterized).
- password (string, required): login password ("password123" in demonstration).
- mass_action (string, required, enum): which mass action to perform in the Actions dropdown. Values sourced from the page: "Delete", "Subscribe to Newsletter", "Unsubscribe from Newsletter", "Assign a Customer Group". Internally we use the visible text for select_change.selectedText.
- selection_mode (string, required, enum): how to select customers before running the action. From demonstrated behaviors we can support: "select_visible" (click Select Visible link), "none" (do not change selection), and "first_3" (click the first three row checkboxes as in step 8). This captures the meaningful variety without adding conditionals.
- customer_group (string, optional): required only when mass_action == "Assign a Customer Group", but the schema cannot express conditional requirement, so we mark it not required and explain in description. Possible values as visible texts: "General", "Wholesale", "VIP Member", "Private Sales Member".
- apply_group_filter (bool, optional): whether to apply the Group filter and Search after the mass action; default=false.
- filter_group (string, optional): visible text of Group filter to use when apply_group_filter is true.

We do NOT parameterize low-level things like which column to sort because the trajectory only clicked Email header once and sorting is not essential to mass actions. We also do not parameterize pagination or export since they are outside the original task.

5) Step Optimization:
- Navigation is a single direct navigation step to /admin/customer/; no need to click menus.
- Login: we rely entirely on deterministic "input" and "click" steps using elementHash/index-derived selectors instead of the previously failing CSS selector. This directly addresses the error: "Selector 'input[name=\"login[username]\"][type=\"text\"]' not found".
- The grid is accessible at /admin/customer/index/ after login; however the app automatically redirects there. We don’t need an additional navigation step; we simply wait for grid controls to be visible.
- For mass actions, we avoid agentic steps because the trajectory already captured stable select and button elements via elementHash. We construct deterministic select_change and click steps.
- The optional filter step is deterministic: Group filter dropdown (elementHash 547d16e240) and Search button (654dbd41a1).
- We omit extraction steps since tool’s purpose is acting, not reading; success can be inferred by Magento’s UI but extraction is not required for subsequent steps.

Given the session, elementHash values used in steps are:
- Login username input: 3597a5c5e6 (index 1).
- Login password input: 1c47a5217e (index 3).
- Login button: 6831836d17 (index 5).
- Notification close link: df76c6ce85 (index 102).
- Row checkbox inputs: 822a6e2ce4 (indices 160–197 etc.).
- Select Visible link: 0eefac88df (indices 131/134 depending on page state).
- Actions dropdown: b202e94e0d (indices 133/136).
- Submit button: 32139f0b8f / 94c3ca62f9 (indices 134/136/137) – same logical button.
- Group selector (mass action): 4a4c64c2db (index 135) – when Assign Group selected.
- Group filter dropdown (in filter row): 547d16e240 (index 150) – used when filtering by group.
- Search button: 654dbd41a1 (index 128).

Selectors are primarily elementHash to avoid ambiguity across similar inputs; indices corroborate but are not directly used in this tool format.

Because the core goal is to perform mass customer actions, the tool’s essential steps are: navigate, login, ensure grid, (optional) close popup, select customers, choose mass action, optionally choose group, submit, optionally filter. No unrelated navigation, export, or pagination is included.
name: magento_admin_mass_customer_actions_v5
description: Automates Magento Admin login and execution of mass customer actions (delete, subscribe/unsubscribe newsletter, assign customer group) on the Manage Customers grid using robust, index- and hash-based selectors instead of brittle CSS selectors.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin customer URL, which shows the login page when not authenticated.
Enter the Magento Admin username into the username input field on the login page.
Enter the Magento Admin password into the password input field on the login page.
Click the Login button to submit the admin login form.
Wait for the Manage Customers grid page to load after login.
Close the notification popup on the Manage Customers grid page to ensure grid controls are interactable.
Apply the requested customer selection strategy before executing the mass action.
steps.task: Based on the parameter selection_mode ('select_visible', 'first_3', or 'none'), perform the corresponding selection on the Manage Customers grid using known elements: for 'select_visible', click the 'Select Visible' link (elementHash 0eefac88df); for 'first_3', click the first three row checkboxes (elementHash 822a6e2ce4 for rows 1–3); for 'none', do nothing and keep current selection. Do not change any other state.

steps.description: Choose the desired mass action from the Actions dropdown using the provided visible text.
When assigning a customer group, select the target group in the Group dropdown using the provided visible text. If customer_group is empty this selection may be ignored by the site.
Click the Submit button to execute the selected mass action on the selected customers.
Wait for the grid to refresh and the mass action to be processed by the server.
Optionally apply a Group filter and search to verify or refine the customer list after the mass action.
steps.task: If apply_group_filter is true, select the provided filter_group value in the Group filter dropdown (elementHash 547d16e240) in the filter row, then click the Search button (elementHash 654dbd41a1). If apply_group_filter is false, do nothing. Do not modify other filters or controls.

input_schema.name: username
input_schema.description: Magento Admin login username to enter into the username field on the login page.

input_schema.name: password
input_schema.description: Magento Admin login password to enter into the password field on the login page.

input_schema.name: mass_action
input_schema.description: Visible text of the mass action to perform from the Actions dropdown on the Manage Customers grid.

input_schema.name: selection_mode
input_schema.description: How to select customers before running the mass action: 'select_visible' clicks the 'Select Visible' link, 'first_3' clicks the first three row checkboxes, 'none' leaves the current selection unchanged.

input_schema.name: customer_group
input_schema.description: Visible text of the customer group to assign when mass_action is 'Assign a Customer Group'. Options include: 'General', 'Wholesale', 'VIP Member', 'Private Sales Member'.

input_schema.name: apply_group_filter
input_schema.description: If true, apply a Group filter and click Search after the mass action completes.

input_schema.name: filter_group
input_schema.description: Visible text of the Group filter option to select in the filter row when apply_group_filter is true.
